small_guidance:
- The conv kernel materializes an [OC=16, BLOCK_OW] accumulator and reloads x for every (kd,kh,kw,ic) — try larger BLOCK_OW (128, 256) with num_warps=8 and add a tile over OH (BLOCK_OH=2 or 4) so each program reuses the same input slab across multiple output rows, amortizing the gather.
- Add autotune configs that vary num_stages (2/3/4) at BLOCK_OW=128/256 and consider BLOCK_OW=OW (33) so the inner masking disappears; also try swapping the loop order so `ic` is outermost and `(kd,kh,kw)` inner, letting the same x value contribute to all kernel taps before reloading.
- Fold the `iw_num // STRIDE` and `(iw_num % STRIDE)==0` math into a precomputed iw_val/iw_valid that's reused across kd/kh (currently recomputed each kw iteration is fine, but hoist `id_val/ih_val` checks; also precompute `n*IC*ID*IH*IW` base offset once).
large_guidance:
- Reformulate as a gather-GEMM in channels-last layout: one program per (N, OD tile, OH tile, OW tile), accumulator shape [BLOCK_SPATIAL, OC], with the K dimension being IC*KD*KH*KW. Pre-pack the weight as [IC*KD*KH*KW, OC] so the inner loop is a `tl.dot` instead of a scalar outer product — this is the biggest headroom since OC=16 is too small for the current outer-product layout to use tensor cores.
- Alternatively, since stride=2 makes only ~1/8 of (kd,kh,kw,ic) combinations valid for any output, use a scatter-add formulation: one program per (N, ID, IH, IW tile) computes `input[n,ic,id,ih,iw] * W[ic,:,:,:,:]` outer products and atomically scatters into the output grid; this halves arithmetic versus the gather form.
- Fuse Swish + GroupNorm reduction: since GroupNorm reduces over (C_per_G=4) channels × OD*OH*OW spatial elements per (N,G), have the conv kernel write swish output and accumulate per-group sum/sumsq into a small auxiliary buffer in the same launch (one atomic per program), eliminating the first reduction pass of the GN kernel.
